summary: Wave 2 backend + frontend smoke tests. Booking cancellation + refund, site material request 4-stage chain, and reminder-engine cron endpoints all pass. 24/24 pytest tests green. Frontend: sidebar entries, /cancellations and /material-requests pages, cancel button + dialog on Sales page, and MR create dialog all render and wire correctly.

minor.issue: No single-unit GET endpoint exists; tests had to filter from /api/units list. Not a bug per se, but adding one would simplify consumers.
Hard-coded limit=50 combined with high notification volume for super_admin makes it possible for older reminders to age out; consider a filter-by-kind query param.

issues: Radix warning: Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent — accessibility gap.
Recharts warning: width(-1)/height(-1) for chart containers — chart container mount race, cosmetic.

action_items: (Optional) Add GET /api/units/{unit_id} single-unit endpoint for direct fetch.
(Optional) Add aria-describedby on cancel/MR/refund DialogContents to silence Radix a11y warning.
(Optional) Add filter-by-kind query param on /api/notifications for large accounts.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3355 lines — well beyond the 700-line guideline; hard to maintain. Recommend splitting into routers (cancellations, material_requests, cron, notifications, installments).

_run_reminders builds `team` and fires N notifications and N emails sequentially inside async loop — for large user bases + many installments this can be slow. Consider bulk insert for notifications and batching email dispatch.

iter13 test 'test_all_14_statuses_in_source' asserts 14 UnitStatus literals but Wave 2 introduced 'cancellation_requested' bringing total to 15. Iter13 test is now stale; should be updated by main agent (kept out-of-scope here since Wave 1 file).
notify() stores field as 'kind' but README/tests may expect 'type' — worth documenting/aligning in an API contract.
Reminder loop iterates all reminable installments and computes offset per call — for scale, an index on due_date + status is worthwhile.
seed_data_creation: Created test project TEST_W2_<runtag>, 8 role users (w2_<role>_<runtag>@example.com), and multiple sold + cancelled + material-request records. Site supervisor assigned to test project via PATCH /users/{id}.

rca_of_the_issue: N/A — all Wave 2 flows behave as specified. Two initial test-run failures were fixture bugs in my test code (using non-existent GET /units/{id} and wrong 'type' field name) — both fixed.
